title: Review: Data (Off-Broadway) starring Karan Bear (Jessie), Brandon Fly...
transcript: Plays about AI and modern technology are really hard to get right because plays take time to write, and this technology is evolving at an alarming rate. So often what ends up happening is you either have a play that feels instantly dated, or you have a play that feels like it's looking too far ahead into the future, bordering on science fiction. Data is the rare play that I feel like actually manages to speak to the technological concerns of today, asking some really interesting ethical questions around data and AI and how it should and should not be used. It follows the employees of a data company working on a highly sensitive project, the specifics of which you don't really learn until about halfway through the play. And our main character of Manisha, played by Karen Brah from Jessie, is caught between two colleagues, one of whom believes in the project and wants to see it come to fruition, and one of whom believes the project is inherently unethical and needs to be stopped. While I found the pacing of the play to be a bit uneven, the conversations that come out of it are genuinely, really fascinating and, quite frankly, a little bit terrifying, because these are definitely conversations that are being had at similar companies around the country and around the world. This play, more than anything, is a warning and a wake up call about what can happen if this technology gets into the wrong Hands assuming it hasn't already
reasoning: Creator praises the play as a rare success in the AI genre and finds the conversations fascinating and timely, though notes uneven pacing. Overall a clear recommendation with a caveat.
